author: Andrew Perez

Elon Musk publicly endorsed "socialist" healthcare before he became the
world's richest man. Now, years later, he's running super PAC ads decrying
Democrats as "socialists" for supporting government-run healthcare.

In Maine, Musk's America PAC is
[attacking](https://d3jqbr7k2eq8xz.cloudfront.net/b2d90adc-6a39-477d-87a4-8e8269479c93.mp4)
Senate candidate Troy Jackson for wanting to "put the government in charge of
your healthcare." One ad, which ran on the streaming service Roku, says "the
socialists know Jackson will rubber stamp their agenda," featuring democratic
socialists Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Zohran Mamdani in the
background. America PAC has also sent door-knockers around Maine to [hand out
leaflets](https://x.com/andrewperezdc/status/2095610764396491097) slamming
Jackson for supporting Medicare for All, which would create a comprehensive,
universal healthcare system.

Musk's group has run other ads
[attacking](https://d3jqbr7k2eq8xz.cloudfront.net/c1eca8c0-4130-4db3-bb87-081f3e209692.mp4)
former Ohio Senator Sherrod Brown as a supporter of "government-run
healthcare," and
[claiming](https://d3jqbr7k2eq8xz.cloudfront.net/316cf239-ffaa-4a65-a448-e3cb5d56dff0.mp4)
former Virginia Congresswoman Elaine Luria will help socialists "ban our
private health insurance." (Neither Brown nor Luria back Medicare for All,
though they [have](https://www.whitehouse.senate.gov/news/release/whitehouse-
brown-cheer-new-public-option-push/)
[both](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2018/10/04/gop-ads-falsely-
depict-democrats-supporters-sanderss-health-plan/)
[supported](https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/465881-sherrod-brown-
terrible-mistake-for-democratic-nominee-to-support-medicare/) public health
insurance options in the past.)

Yes, it is offensive that the world's richest man, a major beneficiary of
[federal contracts](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/13/business/musk-trillionaire-
government-tesla-spacex) and [policy](https://zeteo.com/p/elon-musk-spacex-
ipo-
trillionaire?utm_campaign=23234856710&utm_source=google_ads&utm_medium=cpc&utm_content=189841814802-782839857508&utm_term=&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23234856710&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIpeKax_yElwMV_jQIBR3lHwjeEAAYASAAEgJS3fD_BwE),
would deploy his incomprehensible wealth to spend on U.S. elections - and,
even more, that he would run ads mocking the idea of giving every American
cheaper, improved healthcare coverage, along the lines of what people get in
other wealthy, industrialized nations.

But there's also always a tweet. Less than a decade ago, Musk openly touted
the idea of government-run, "socialist" healthcare - saying it has majority
support - on Twitter, the social media platform he now owns.
